Yes: the matching paper is Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation by Woosung Koh, Hyunsoo Lee, Kyungjae Lee, et al. [1] It targets small models specifically, arguing that prior self-distillation fine-tuning fails on smaller models because it depends on strong in-context learning and instruction-following abilities. [1]

The paper introduces Synthetic Self-Distillation (SynthSelf), which uses a minimally larger, same-family aligner to produce in-distribution rewrites for the small model, combined with off-policy supervision and rejection sampling. [1] According to the abstract, SynthSelf consistently outperforms six baselines across multiple acquisition datasets, retention benchmarks, and three small model scales, aiming at effective continual learning for low-latency, on-device small models. [1]
